title: edge-gateway-airgap-bridge-architecture-and-operational-playbook-2026
author: Lena Park
body:
Overview:

This document describes the Edge Gateway (aka Airgap Bridge) reference architecture for Redwood private deployments that require a minimal, auditable outbound surface to Redwood control services while keeping customer inference workloads on-prem or inside a VPC with strict egress controls. It combines network hardening, telemetry proxying, secure model updates, and a prescriptive day-2 operational playbook for upgrades and rollback. Use this page when designing new private deployments that must: maintain air-gapped controls, allow limited signed model and config updates, and provide safe live-migration / rollback paths.

Key goals:
- Keep inference workloads isolated (no inbound access from Redwood)
- Allow controlled, auditable outbound-only channels for: telemetry, package updates, and KMS proxying
- Provide deterministic upgrade and rollback procedures with preflight checks
- Minimize operational blast radius with per-cluster edge gateways and clear ownership

Architecture summary:

At a high level the Edge Gateway sits in a hardened DMZ or edge subnet controlled by the customer. It acts as a single outbound egress proxy and update broker for one or more private inference clusters. Critical features: signed artifact validation, mTLS to Redwood control plane (optional), local caching for model packages and KV cache snapshots, configurable telemetry aggregation, and local KMS proxying for envelope encryption.

ASCII diagram (text):

Customer VPC / On-Prem Network:

  [Private Inference Cluster A]   [Private Inference Cluster B]
           |                          |
           \-----> [Edge Gateway (egress DMZ)] -----> [Redwood Control Plane (API + Artifact CDN)]
                                 |
                                 ---> [Telemetry Sink (customer ELK / Splunk)]
                                 ---> [Optional KMS Proxy (HSM / KMS)]

Component descriptions:

1) Edge Gateway (primary component)
- Responsibilities: outbound-only broker for model bundles, rollout policy enforcement, local artifact cache, telemetry batching, certificate rotation agent, local health-checks and canary coordination.
- Recommended placement: single AZ subnet with strict NSG/ACLs. One gateway may serve multiple clusters in same region; prefer 1:1 when customers require strong isolation.

2) Artifact cache and verifier
- Stores signed model bundles and runtime packages.
- Verifies signatures with Redwood public keys OR customer-trusted CA.
- Supports delta updates to reduce bandwidth.

3) KMS proxy (optional)
- Accepts requests from runtime nodes for envelope encryption/decryption and forwards to customer KMS/HSM.
- Provides auditing and short-lived credentials; the gateway never stores long-term KMS keys.

4) Telemetry aggregator
- Batches metrics/logs/traces and forwards on schedule or size thresholds.
- Supports local retention policy for compliance.

Network & firewall ports (minimum):

| Source | Destination | Port/Proto | Purpose |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Inference Cluster -> Edge Gateway | edge-gateway.local | 8443/TCP | gRPC control plane & healthchecks (mutual TLS) |
| Edge Gateway -> Redwood CDN/API | api.redwood.example.net | 443/TCP | Artifacts, control plane API (egress only) |
| Edge Gateway -> Customer KMS/HSM | kms.corp.local | 443/TCP or custom | Envelope ops (optional) |
| Edge Gateway -> Customer Telemetry | splunk.corp.local | 8088/TCP | Batched logs/metrics |
| Operator Workstation -> Edge Gateway | edge-gateway-admin.local | 22/TCP, 8444/TCP | Admin access via jumpbox (restricted) |

Security controls and hardening checklist:
- TLS: Enforce mTLS for all internal connections; validate both client and server certificates.
- FIPS/KMS: When required, configure KMS proxy to use HSM-backed keys.
- Hardening: apply CIS Linux benchmark, minimize installed packages, run EDR/agent as per customer policy.
- Least privilege: edge gateway service accounts grant only necessary decryption/signature verification rights.
- Audit: immutable logs for artifact origins, validation decisions, and operator interactions.

Preflight requirements (customer must provide):
- Outbound allowlist to: api.redwood.example.net (443) and artifact CDN CIDR (provided per-deployment).
- Host with at least 8 vCPU, 32 GiB RAM, 200 GiB NVMe or equivalent for artifact cache.
- TLS certificate chain or acceptance of Redwood-signed certs (agreement signed).
- Access to customer telemetry endpoint or agreed retention for Redwood-sent telemetry.

Deployment procedure (step-by-step):

1) Provision edge gateway host(s) in DMZ subnet and confirm hardened baseline.
2) Install gateway package (signed) and verify checksum/signature: 

   curl -fL https://cdn.redwood.example.net/gateway/v1.2.3/gateway.tar.gz -o /tmp/gateway.tar.gz
   curl -fL https://cdn.redwood.example.net/gateway/v1.2.3/gateway.tar.gz.sig -o /tmp/gateway.tar.gz.sig
   gpg --import redwood-release.pub
   gpg --verify /tmp/gateway.tar.gz.sig /tmp/gateway.tar.gz

3) Configure gateway.yaml (example snippet):

   apiVersion: v1
   edgeGateway:
     listen: 0.0.0.0:8443
     tls:
       certPath: /etc/ssl/edge/tls.crt
       keyPath: /etc/ssl/edge/tls.key
     controlPlaneEndpoint: https://api.redwood.example.net
     artifactCacheDir: /var/lib/redwood/artifacts
     telemetry:
       endpoint: https://splunk.corp.local:8088/event
       batchSize: 1000

4) Validate local health and connectivity (automated checks):
- smoke-checks: verify signature validation, outbound TLS handshake to control plane, KMS proxy reachability (if configured).
- Run: redwood-edgectl health-check --preflight

5) Register gateway with customer control records and limit operator ACLs.

Rollout & upgrade strategy (safe-by-default):

- Blue/Green for gateway software: run a second gateway instance in parallel and switch routing after health checks pass.
- Canary model rollouts: deliver model bundles to artifact cache with "canary=true" metadata; route 1–5% of traffic initially.
- Signed bundles only: no unsigned artifacts are accepted unless explicit emergency policy is enacted and logged.

Upgrade procedure (example):
1) Push gateway package to artifact cache with 'candidate' tag.
2) Validate signed package on a staging gateway.
3) Promote to canary gateway(s), run 24–72 hour canary with SLO telemetry monitoring.
4) If canary is healthy, schedule fully automated cutover during low-traffic window.

Rollback procedure (fast path):
- If health checks or SLO regressions exceed thresholds (see SLOs below), the gateway will automatically switch routing back to the last healthy gateway image and revoke the candidate bundle.
- Manual rollback steps: 
  1. Run: redwood-edgectl rollback --target-image v1.2.2
  2. Confirm health: redwood-edgectl health-check
  3. Revoke candidate: redwood-edgectl revoke-artifact --id <artifact-id>

SLOs, alerts and thresholds (recommended defaults):
- Gateway availability: 99.95% (per-month)
- Artifact verification latency: 95th percentile < 200 ms (on LAN)
- Telemetry delivery: 99% of batches delivered within 60s
- Alerting: Pager if availability < 99.9% for 10 min, or verification latency > 500 ms for 5% of requests over 15 min window.

Day-2 operational playbook (runbook snippets):

Healthcheck failure: artifact verification error rate > 1%
1) Escalation: on-call infra -> edge-gateway-owner -> security on-call.
2) Actions:
   - Check gateway logs: journalctl -u redwood-edge -n 500
   - Confirm signature key expiry: /etc/ssl/redwood/pubkey.pem
   - Re-sync public keys: redwood-edgectl refresh-keys
   - If originating from CDN outage: next step is to serve from local artifact cache and increase TTL for cached bundles.

Telemetry backlog alert: backlog > 1M events or > 24 hours retention
1) Triage: verify disk usage at /var/lib/redwood/telemetry
2) Temporarily increase batch interval and flush manually: redwood-edgectl telemetry flush --now
3) If persistent, increase retention or scale gateway workers and open an incident.

Certificate rotation (recommended cadence): every 30 days for mTLS certs; every 90 days for gateway server certs unless customer policy dictates otherwise. Rotation steps:
- Generate CSR on gateway (or use ACME if allowed).
- Submit to certificate authority and install cert to /etc/ssl/edge/
- Trigger rotation: redwood-edgectl cert-rotate --cert /etc/ssl/edge/tls.crt --key /etc/ssl/edge/tls.key

Customer requirements checklist (table):

| Category | Minimum spec / requirement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hosts | 8 vCPU, 32 GiB RAM, 200 GiB NVMe | 2x for HA recommended |
| Network | Outbound to api.redwood.example.net:443 and artifact CDN | Allowlist required; provide CIDR to customer before deploy |
| Storage | 200 GiB local cache, backup to NFS optional | SSD recommended for artifact unpacking |
| Security | Ability to run mTLS and customer KMS/HSM integration | Customer must provide CA certs and KMS endpoint |
| Compliance | Local log retention policy, ability to export audit logs | Align with customer retention SLA |

Packaging considerations for airgapped installs:
- Provide an airgap bundle with all runtime packages, OS dependencies, and install scripts.
- Include a "bootstrap" installer that validates checksums and verifies signatures offline.
- Provide a package manifest (SHA256) and a simple local artifact server container image.

Example local bootstrap command (airgap host):

   sudo tar xzf redwood-edge-airgap-1.2.3.tar.gz -C /opt/redwood
   sudo /opt/redwood/install.sh --offline --manifest /opt/redwood/manifest.json

Operational ownership and support matrix:
- Customer: network ACLs, KMS, telemetry endpoint, physical hosts, baseline OS hardening.
- Redwood: gateway software, artifact signing keys, control plane API, troubleshooting support per contract.

Risk register & mitigations (high level):
- Stale public keys -> mitigation: automated weekly key rotation and heartbeat with signature test.
- Artifact poisoning -> mitigation: require multi-signature for high-risk bundles; validate provenance metadata.
- KMS availability -> mitigation: local cache of envelope keys for short TTL with strong audit trails.

References and further reading:
- Hybrid control plane reference architecture (internal): /confluence/eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures/hybrid-control-plane-reference-architecture-2026
- Private deploy compliance checklist (internal): /confluence/eng-private-deployments/customer-requirements-library/private-deploy-compliance-and-evidence-checklist-2025

Appendix: quick troubleshooting commands
- Check gateway health: redwood-edgectl health-check --json
- List cached artifacts: redwood-edgectl artifacts list --format table
- Force artifact verification: redwood-edgectl artifacts verify --id <artifact-id>
- Rotate keys manually: redwood-edgectl refresh-keys --force
